Nuno Mendes acknowledged the difficulties Paris Saint-Germain faced in their 2-2 draw against Roma at the Parc des Princes.

The Portuguese full-back, playing in the mixed zone, praised the tactical work of Gian Piero Gasperini’s team, which caused considerable difficulty for the French and European champions with intense pressing and precise organization.

It has been revealed that “There are teams that will try to play this way in the future, and we’ll be ready. We already know what we have to do for the full 90 minutes. They caused our team a lot of problems, but I think we managed to overcome their pressure at times.”.

In a recent development, “There were also moments when they managed to find space, win the ball back, and cause us problems. They were one of the most difficult teams to face. We have our own way of playing, and we never change. They analyzed it carefully, just as we had studied Roma, but they still managed to create a lot of problems for us. There are games where we can’t always be at our best, but we’ll keep trying.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leeds United have a number of players out on loan this season, with a mixture of senior stars and academy prospects looking to make an impression away from Elland Road.
  • There are high-profile names looking to rediscover their form, youngsters trying to catch Daniel Farke’s attention and a few with a question mark over what comes next.
  • Recent findings suggest that we’ve taken a look at all eight Leeds loanees to see how they’re getting on this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leeds United have a number of players out on loan this season, with a mixture of senior stars and academy prospects looking to make an impression away from Elland Road.

There are high-profile names looking to rediscover their form, youngsters trying to catch Daniel Farke’s attention and a few with a question mark over what comes next.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve taken a look at all eight Leeds loanees to see how they’re getting on this season. Note: We haven’t included the academy players sent to non-league clubs.

Leeds loan manager Andrew Taylor explicitly cited the 18-year-old striker, saying that “the focus is very much to go and get games in a first-team environment to ultimately come back to our first team squad.”.

The latest member of the Gray dynasty was on a bit of a hiding to nothing when he went out on loan to doomed Rotherham United last season, but it no doubt would’ve been invaluable experience for an immensely exciting young talent.

This season the teenager has stayed in South Yorkshire, but this time to a club with ambitions at the right end of the League One table. The Owls hit rock bottom last term but are looking to be on their way back up.

It has been revealed that it hasn’t all been plain sailing for Gray, though, with just one goal so far. He also appears to have been pushed to the periphery by Dave Challinor.

A January loan move elsewhere has been mooted in the local press, but it’s still early days. The hectic December schedule ought to give the 18-year-old chances to win the new boss around.

The Cardiff City academy graduate made waves by making his senior international debut for Wales before he ever made a first-team appearance for his club.

Industry observers note that crew eventually made his Leeds debut with a brief cameo to see out a 3-0 Championship victory over Plymouth Argyle. No second appearance followed, and he’s spent the past couple of years gaining experience in a series of loans.

After a couple of stints with Doncaster Rovers, the midfielder has dropped down to League Two with Walsall. He’s been in and out of the starting XI under Lee Grant, but is identifying this as a season to really kick on.

“Just inconsistency within myself really,” Crew told the Express & Star about where he’s looking to improve.

“Inconsistency in performances and inconsistency in the amount of minutes that I was getting.

“That’s down to me to change it and hopefully this season I can with hard work and games like this today, going for the full 90 minutes and really showing that I’m consistent in performances in and out of possession.

Industry observers note that “It’s a great place for that next step, with the belief that the gaffer puts into everyone, but especially me. And that the team-mates around me, it’s definitely a place where I feel that I can progress and I’m enjoying my football a lot.”.

We haven’t included the youngsters that Leeds have sent out to clubs like Hebburn Town, Hebburn Town and Scarborough Athletic, but Lopata-White just about makes the cut-off point out at Altrincham in the National League.

The 21-year-old centre-back has been a regular fixture for the midtable Robins, who are well in the mix for a play-off spot.

He’s been a regular and started in a number of wins, but recently found himself suspended after getting a straight red in the early minutes of a 4-0 defeat away to Harrogate Town.

In a recent development, west Ham’s strategy doesn’t appear the most imaginative, but on paper was sensible. In Scott Parker, they’ve got a manager who has three promotions in as many attempts, while in Piroe they brought in the most proven Championship goalscorer on the market.

According to recent reports, but things aren’t quite going to plan. The Hammers are yet to win under Parker and find themselves languishing in the bottom half of the table. Piroe has one goal in his last 11 appearances.

Search Piroe’s name on social media – never the most level-headed barometer, admittedly – and you’ll no doubt come across posts by irate West Ham fans wondering why they signed such a donkey.

Piroe’s limitations always made it unlikely he’d be a success in the Premier League, but anyone who watched him at Leeds will be surprised he’s struggling to find the back of the net in the second tier.

There is a reported £8million purchase obligation dependent on promotion, but that looks like a massive ‘if’ at present.

Strangely enough, Leeds actually went unbeaten when the Belgian started last season (six wins, three draws), but he never nailed down a first-team place and was knocked down the pecking order following the signing of Nico Elvedi in the summer.

According to recent reports, he’s back in the Bundesliga and getting the minutes he was targeting with Hamburg, but defeats have been a bit more frequent this season. A 4-0 defeat at Werder Bremen at the weekend was particularly chastening.

Things didn’t quite work out for him at Elland Road, but the experienced goalkeeper has found his feet since leaving Leeds.

Torino might be struggling in the lower half of the table, but Perri has been one of their brighter performers. He made nine saves in a 1-0 defeat to Napoli at the weekend, doing his best to keep the scoreline respectable, and his performances have earned him a Brazil call-up from Carlo Ancelotti earlier this month.

Torino have a reported €14million purchase option, which you’d expect them to seriously consider exercising if he keeps this up.

“Sometimes you’re giving them a loan to a try and increase the value for a return on an investment, or you’re just giving them a chance to go and get exposure,” the club’s loan manager told the official website.

“They go out and get men’s football and it’s gaining traction.”.

While not naming him, you’d imagine that Chambers belongs in this camp.

The Leeds-born Scotland youth international, 19, is getting his first experience of senior men’s football out at Northampton Town.

Unfortunately that has been hard to come by, and he’s rarely made the Cobblers’ matchday squad since September.

Like Piroe, the writing was on the wall for Gnonto’s immediate future at Leeds. He was rarely trusted to start games by Farke.

The pint-sized winger has returned to Italy for the first time since leaving Inter Milan’s youth set-up as a boy. He’s joined a veritable hodgepodge of former Premier League players at Fiorentina, sharing a dressing room with David de Gea, Radu Dragusin, Beto and Alex Jimenez.

The somewhat scattergun recruitment approach has not worked wonders, with La Viola down near the relegation zone after notching just two wins all season.

Italy legend Fabio Grosso was sacked in early September, but Paolo Vanoli has struggled to turn things around.

It has been revealed that gnonto is yet to score or assist in 10 Serie A appearances, but he did notch his first goal for the club in a 3-0 Coppa Italia victory over second-tier Pisa. He was handed a rare start in their last outing, a disastrous 3-0 defeat to Monza.

During Leeds’ rare dips of form, or when things got a bit stodgy and predictable, there was a not inconsiderable portion of the Leeds fanbase that loudly questioned why Farke didn’t really fancy Ramazani.

Sources indicate that the Belgian winger, perhaps by dint of not playing much, had a perceived X Factor that Leeds apparently lacked. We’re seeing parallels with the lesser-spotted Jean-Matteo Bahoya this season.

We’ll see how the Bahoya situation plays out, but you look at the direction of travel for Ramazani and Farke’s scepticism has probably been vindicated on that front.

According to recent reports, the Belgian winger had his moments at Valencia last season, but now finds himself back in the Championship at Burnley. To be fair, he recently scored in three successive outings and has been a rare bright spark for the basket case Clarets, but there’s little to suggest he deserved more minutes at his parent club.

Burnley have won just once all season and find themselves second bottom of the table. They’ll need Ramazani to keep delivering if they’re to avoid the dreaded double drop.

The 1997-born player moved to the Rossoblu on loan this summer with an option to buy for €17 million, an option that will never be exercised and forces Roma to take direct interest, to avoid further devaluing a €41 million investment.

In a recent development, now Valencia are serious and considering signing Dovbyk. One of the challenges to be resolved is his €3 million net salary, of which €2.5 million is paid by the Rossoblu. The Spanish club is expected to pay half.

According to Il Resto del Carlino, recent news has revealed direct contact between the Spanish club and the Ukrainian player, who has reportedly expressed interest in a return to La Liga.

According to recent reports, the 1997-born player has left a lasting impression, having scored 24 goals for Girona. Valencia has initiated initial discussions with Roma to understand potential terms and costs: approval will be needed from Bologna, which will pay Dovbyk €2.5 million of his €3 million net salary.

#152982. How a green economy could help reverse climate change

How a green economy could help reverse climate change

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1443 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Human civilization is right now profoundly unsustainable.
  • If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.
  • In a recent development, it's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Human civilization is right now profoundly unsustainable. Earth has already crossed seven of the nine planetary boundaries critical for sustaining life, including climate change, ocean acidification and biosphere integrity.

If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.

In a recent development, it's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change. That's where the idea of green growth comes in.

It has been revealed that its promise is to keep growing the economy while reducing emissions and resource use. That involves, for instance, running factories, businesses and homes on wind, solar and other green energy instead of coal and gas, replacing gas-fired furnaces with heat pumps and  recycling and reusing resources and raw materials.

Recent findings suggest that "Basically, the idea is: business as usual, but with more sustainable technologies," mentioned Helmut Haberl, a social ecology professor at BOKU University in Vienna. Along with his colleagues, he published a major report in 2020 evaluating more than 800 studies on green growth.

Recent findings suggest that in principle, the world's economic output could continue to grow in the long term and generate significantly fewer emissions from the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas. That's been shown in scenarios modeled by researchers with the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, or IPCC.

Thanks to renewable energy and green technologies, those scenarios have already become reality in several countries and regions.

Sources indicate that the economies of developed countries like the United Kingdom, the United States, Japanand Australia have experienced years of growth alongside sinking CO2 emissions. That's even when offshore production is included.

In the European Union, the bloc-wide economy has grown by more than 70% since 1990. Meanwhile, the EU's carbon emissions have dropped by around 40%.

But such a complete decoupling of growth and emissions is, according to Haberl and his fellow researchers, relatively rare.

In India, and in several countries in Africa and Southeast Asia, economies are becoming more efficient. But while economic performance is outpacing emissions growth, emissions are still rising in those countries and globally. This is not compatible with preventing the worst impacts of climate change.

"That doesn't mean, however, that it couldn't work in the future," said Haberl, referring to decoupling of growth and emissions.

And even though economic growth has been shown to be compatible with emissions reduction, eliminating all greenhouse gases from a polluting industry like steel or chemicals is complicated.

These sectors don't just release emissions by burning fossil fuels for energy; carbon is also a key part of the chemical processes used to create their products, notably in the steel industry.

Replacing it with greener substitutes, or an alternative energy source like green hydrogen, requires significant investment.

There's another hurdle: the world's high consumption of resources. A productive economy depends on many raw materials and other products: ores, chemicals, wood, cement, glass and agricultural products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Many countries are now using green technologies to reduce the amount of resources needed to manufacture a product, for example, and are making their economies more efficient.

But that doesn't mean overall fewer resources are being used because falling costs can encourage businesses to produce more things and people to consume more. This can partially offset green savings and is called the rebound effect.

The British economy has been growing for years, emissions have been dropping and efficiency has increased, but the UK still used 7% more resources in 2023 than it did in 2001.

Sources indicate that global resource consumption has tripled over the last 50 years. If the world continues on the current pathway, that could increase by another 60% by 2060. It remains unclear whether green growth can deliver the emissions and resource reductions needed to stop climate change and biodiversity loss rapidly enough.

"We really need to move beyond efficiency gains in our existing production practices to look more broadly at what we consume," said Catherine Ganzleben, a sustainability and fair transitions expert at the European Environment Agency.

She told DW that people also need to reconsider how they consume and whether they really need to own everything they use in their daily life — cars, for example.

"But we can shift towards models where we share cars, so we pool our resources and have significantly lower resources per person through sharing the goods that we need.".

Some researchers have concluded that unrestricted economic growth is no longer possible in the long term, even if it's sustainable.

Instead, they've called for degrowth. This posits slower economic growth, no growth at all or even negative growth, so that the world's ecosystems and the climate have a chance to recover and stabilize.

In a recent development, that applies mainly to economies in richer countries, which would need to take targeted steps to reduce their energy and resource use. Poorer countries would continue to grow until their economies and quality of life improve significantly.

In a recent development, under the degrowth theory, a society's prosperity is not measured solely by the growth of its gross domestic product, but by values such as quality of life, education and community. The idea is that once countries develop to a certain point, additional growth doesn't translate into greater well-being.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the concept is based on the idea that human well-being and ecological sustainability is only possible in the long term with a planned, socially just reduction of material production and resource consumption. Degrowth advocates argue this would be preferable to an unplanned and potentially catastrophic economic contraction caused by escalating climate extremes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A 2020 study by researchers from the universities of Leeds and Lausanne indicated that the concept of degrowth supported the world's climate goals — and that a high quality of life didn't have to be sacrificed in exchange for a significantly lower consumption of energy and resources.

However, there is still no conclusive evidence that an entire modern economy could continue to function entirely on the degrowth principles in the long term.

Nevertheless, Haberl doesn't assume that an environmentally friendly economic model automatically goes hand in hand with sacrifice, arguing instead for a needs-based economy.

"A society isn't necessarily better off when it's producing more goods and services," he said. It all depends on how prosperity and quality of life are measured in the future, and how states decide to do business.

Recent findings suggest that today, a successful economy is measured by the growth of a country's gross domestic product — put simply, the worth of all of its goods and services. This calculation doesn't account for income distribution, unpaid work, quality of life or environmental damage.

It has been revealed that "The highest possible real incomes for every individual would probably not be compatible with ecological goals in the long term," remarked Haberl. "On the other hand, an increase in prosperity — related to a higher quality of life — would be.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An analysis by the European Environment Agency (EEA) pointed out that the idea of steady growth is part of the world's economic cycle, and deeply anchored in our institutions, norms and societal discourse. The job market and tax system are also closely tied to gross domestic product growth. A shrinking economy would therefore require a fundamental shift in our way of thinking.

According to recent reports, countries face a dilemma: a steadily growing economy is not compatible with ecological goals, according to the EEA. On the other side, a sharp decline in growth could trigger enormous social upheaval.

And the correlation is much more complex than the idea of "less is more," as highlighted by an EEA study in November 2021. "The fact that GDP growth has been harmful for the environment does not necessarily mean that declining GDP would be good for the environment," noted the report.

Sources indicate that achieving green growth while respecting environmental limits would require an "unprecedented decoupling of economic activity from environmental and climate pressures. Whether this is feasible is right now uncertain.".

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From a future investment to a potential transfer problem: Robinio Vaz’s time away from Roma risks ending sooner than expected.

The French striker, who moved to Hull City during the final days of the summer transfer window, has failed to establish a significant role in the English side.

According to Tuttomercatoweb.com, the Premier League club is even considering terminating his loan deal early.

Roma acquired Robinio Vaz from Marseille last January for approximately €25 million, banking on the qualities of the 2007-born striker, considered an interesting prospect.

The deal was designed with the player’s future development in mind, but the size of the investment also suggested a potential immediate contribution.

In the second half of the season, however, the Frenchman failed to convince Gian Piero Gasperini, finding very few opportunities to shine. After spending the summer in Rome, the club therefore chose to send him out on loan to help him develop through increased use.

The agreement with Hull City included a €2 million loan with a €30 million option to buy, a deal that could have guaranteed Roma a significant financial return in the event of positive performances. However, things aren’t going as expected.

Vaz continues to find little playing time, and the English club isn’t reportedly considering a permanent purchase of the player.

Instead, the possibility of terminating the deal during the next transfer window has emerged, potentially returning the striker to the Giallorossi early.

Roma is also reportedly dissatisfied with the situation, especially since the lack of playing time risks further slowing the young Frenchman’s development and compromising his value.

The initial goal of the loan was to allow Vaz to gain experience and demonstrate his qualities more consistently, but so far the move to England hasn’t yielded the desired results.

Ranking the 10 best rivalries in English football ahead of Merseyside derby

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s another significant derby this weekend in the Premier League as Everton host Liverpool, which has got us thinking: what are the 10 best rivalries in English football?
  • To set some ground rules, we have mentioned rivalries rather than derbies, so the pedants amongst you can’t complain if the two clubs are not geographically right next to each other.
  • We’ve also ranked them on a mix of the history, the entertainment of recent games, the fanbases and their overall head-to-head records.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s another significant derby this weekend in the Premier League as Everton host Liverpool, which has got us thinking: what are the 10 best rivalries in English football?

To set some ground rules, we have mentioned rivalries rather than derbies, so the pedants amongst you can’t complain if the two clubs are not geographically right next to each other.

We’ve also ranked them on a mix of the history, the entertainment of recent games, the fanbases and their overall head-to-head records.

With those rules in mind, here are our top 10:.

This rivalry is fairly low simply because the games in recent years have been borefests.

After Portsmouth’s drop down the pyramid, the two South Coast clubs only played each other once in 12 years, which was a 4-0 League Cup thumping in 2019, but the 2025-26 season marked the first time the two clubs have been in the same division for over a decade.

Unfortunately, the games have just not lived up to expectations. The first was 0-0 before the second was 1-1. The two have already played each other this season and Southampton won 1-0.

Happily though, it is a derby with a lot of passion behind it and they do hate each other. Saints fans call Portsmouth fans Skates. Pompey respond back with Scummers.

It’s a good derby with passionate fanbases, if only the football lived up to it.

City’s long-standing position as the second-best club in Manchester makes this rank a little low, but even before the takeover, it was a heated rivalry.

Industry observers note that in the old days, City fans would revel at the chance to show United fans that they were the true Mancunians. They took pride in being the less successful club and a derby day win felt like a league title.

Predictably, United have the better head-to-head record with 81 games won to City’s 64.

The Steel City derby is often slept on as one of the best in the country.

In a recent development, for a start, the two sets of fans absolutely despise each other. There have also been memorable matches that live long in their supporters’ memories.

Sources indicate that after Wednesday beat United 4-0 on the 26th of December 1979, it was nicknamed the Boxing Day Massacre and is still brought up to this day. Wednesday also beat United 2-1 in the 1993 FA Cup semi-final.

According to recent reports, it does fall down the ranking a little simply because it has been very one-sided of late. Wednesday have not won since 2012 and the Blades have won the past four meetings.

It does, though, help when the manager buys into it and local boy Chris Wilder was pictured dancing on a pub table when the Blades won 1-0 in November 2024.

Residents of Liverpool usually have an us-against-the-world view but they do look inwards when it comes to derby day.

Their grounds used to be separated by a park and the atmospheres are usually excellent. The only problem is that it is very one-sided.

The two were quite even, especially when both were amongst the best clubs in England, but Everton’s decline has given Liverpool the chance to rack up almost 40 more wins than their opponents.

According to recent reports, it does still produce memorable moments. James Tarkowski’s excellent hit to rescue a point in the final game at Goodison is the kind of thing that will be remembered for decades to come.

There are a huge number of fierce derbies in the Birmingham and Black Country area, but the pick of the bunch is Villa v Birmingham.

They are the biggest clubs in England’s second biggest city While a fan running on the pitch to punch Jack Grealish is obviously moronic, it does speak volumes of the hatred between the two sets of supporters.

We have a sneaky admiration for Dion Dublin headbutting Robbie Savage back in 2003 too.

The 2010 League Cup meeting is one of the most memorable recent encounters but sadly the two have not played each other since 2019.

There’s nothing like 600 years of history to fuel a rivalry.

Leeds United vs Manchester United is the modern Wars of the Roses with the Yorkshire and Lancashire opponents hating everything to do with the other.

It was under two legendary managers that the rivalry really gained with Don Revie’s Leeds and Matt Busby’s Manchester United at their peak in the 1960s.

Industry observers note that there’s also Eric Cantona who was sold to United from Leeds in 1992. Future players Rio Ferdinand and Alan Smith were vilified for doing the same.

Even Sir Alex Ferguson stated the ferocity of games against Leeds was never matched.

West Ham’s return to the Championship set up a long-awaited meeting with Millwall in what is one of England’s oldest and fiercest rivalries.

The two both have working-class origins dating back to the dockyards and acts of violence over decades have made it a poisonous relationship.

Sources indicate that millwall fans hate West Ham fans. West Ham fans hate Millwall fans. It’s as simple as that.

The September meeting this season did not disappoint. Millwall took a 2-0 lead before West Ham equalised in the 80th. An 89th-minute red card completed the derby bingo card.

Industry observers note that it is also very close on the overall head-to-head. Millwall have the advantage with 22 wins to 19 for the Hammers.

The Tyne-Wear derby is easily one of the best in the country.

The grounds are only 10 miles apart, meaning that even though it is two cities facing off, there is a very local feel about it.

It is equally poised with Sunderland’s 55 wins to Newcastle’s 54 and it is a fixture that ebbs and flows in terms of dominance. Even when they were facing relegation year after year, the Black Cats found a way of beating their local rivals throughout the 2010s and Newcastle have not recorded a league win since 2011.

Before that, the Black and Whites enjoyed a run of five wins in a row to start the 21st century.

It has been revealed that the two fanbases also provide plenty of passion and players have a chance to become instant legends. Just ask Brian Brobbey.

The North London rivalry may not be as fierce as others around England, but in terms of a game, it almost always delivers.

Recent findings suggest that in recent times, both clubs have had their dominant periods. Arsenal are Harry Kane’s second favourite team to score against, with the former Spurs striker scoring in five consecutive league games.

Now that he is in Munich, Arsenal have wrestled control of the fixture with five wins in the last five games.

Recent findings suggest that but it is a fixture that tends to not be cagey and instead be frantic, end-to-end action. Players like Emmanuel Adebayor and Sol Campbell have also added fuel to the fire.

It’s the biggest rivalry in English football with the two biggest clubs, for no one has won more league titles than these two.

These near-neighbouring cities first played each other in 1894 and for such a long rivalry the matches are also really well balanced with United having won 93 and Liverpool 83.

It has though been a good few years since both teams were at their best and you’d have to go back to the early 2000s for that sort of elite-level clash.

The games do tend to be rather good. There’s been at least three goals in the last seven matches with a range of results.

And then there’s the fanbases. The corporate world of the modern Premier League has diluted the atmospheres somewhat but both stadiums can feel like cauldrons if given the proper encouragement.

From the January transfer window to Gasperini’s future, including the new stadium and the centenary.

These will be important days for Roma, with Ryan Friedkin expected in the capital starting tomorrow.

As reported by ‘gazzetta.it’, the club’s General Assembly will take place on Friday, November 27th, at Trigoria, a series of meetings to outline the club’s strategies.

Industry observers note that the priority is the winter transfer window, now upon us. Gasperini would like two reinforcements: a left winger and the much-sought-after right-footed attacking midfielder to deploy on the left.

D’Amico and CEO Galantic will have to determine the room for maneuver and whether it will be necessary to sacrifice any players to make incoming investments.

The most viable option seems to be the one already explored with Malen: financially sustainable deals, through onerous loans with an option or obligation to buy, without particularly expensive investments.

Recent findings suggest that the future of Gian Piero Gasperini could also be among the topics of the meetings. It’s not out of the question that discussions could begin regarding an extension of the coach’s contract, which currently expires on June 30, 2028.

According to recent reports, finally, the new stadium project will be discussed. The owners’ goal remains to lay the first stone by next spring, possibly in April, in the year of Roma’s centenary. The club’s centenary celebrations could also be another topic discussed at Trigoria.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

Recent findings suggest that this was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

Sources indicate that the atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

In a recent development, this was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

Industry observers note that “I have to take the responsibility,” he noted. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the proposal. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

In a recent development, “As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the proposal disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it shows.”.

Newcastle looked listless, clueless and alarmingly devoid of belief in what they were being asked to do. They have the unmistakable whiff of a team in decline.

It has been revealed that if they do not start playing a lot better, they will be worried about a relegation battle. It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

Concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight fresh signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat swiftly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

There was no fluency and no threat. The first groans were heard inside 15 minutes as another pass was hoisted harmlessly into the air. They grew more widespread and more frequent.

Everton, just as they had in their Carabao Cup win last week, looked comfortable. Recognising how easy it was to nullify Newcastle’s game proposal, they offered an attacking threat of their own.

A rising shot from Merlin Röhl briefly had goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek worried. A free-kick into the Newcastle box caused panic. James Tarkowski won the first header, but Thierno Barry swung and missed with his left foot.

Industry observers note that the groans began to turn into boos and whistles. Jaissle’s side could barely string more than two passes together. It felt precarious.

In a recent development, this is not an easy place to play football when the crowd airs its displeasure. As the first half limped on, there were players in black and white who looked like they could not handle the pressure.

According to recent reports, it was a horrible game of football. With the last kick of the half, Everton should have taken the lead, Harrison Armstrong picked out Barry inside the box, but he made a mess of the finish. The referee’s whistle was accompanied by boos and a scream of “sort it out” from behind Jaissle’s technical area.

He did not follow those blunt instructions. Everton took the lead in such simple fashion and all Jaissle and his coaching staff could do was shake their heads at each other. Tyrique George was played in far too easily from a free-kick but his shot should have been saved by Hornicek. It was straight at the Czech, but it went through him and it left Barry with a tap in. Newcastle appealed for both a foul on Fabian Schar and an offside but got neither.

Dewsbury-Hall clips a dangerous ball in from the left and picks out O’Brien at the back post but the defender cannot guide his header on target. That was whilst Hall was still off and Barnes was operating as a temporary left-back.

Hall has received some treatment to his back and is now back to his feet.

There will be just two added minutes.

Hall has stayed down after Barry collided into the back of the Newcastle left-back going up for a header.

It has been revealed that george is dispossessed inside his own half before Willock plays it forward to Joelinton. The Brazilian takes one touch before shooting from just outside the box but his effort flies wide of Pickford’s left post. Joelinton struck it powerfully but cut cross the ball too much.

Barnes cuts inside from the left and drives across the face of the penalty area. His shot is semi-blocked by Branthwaite and loops into the air towards his own goal. Pickford takes no risks and palms it over his own bar. Hall’s delivery is headed on by Burn but then cleared by Mykolenko.

Garner is the one to take it but his effort is blocked by the wall. He tried to beat Hornicek at his near post rather than go completely over the wall but the end of the wall still blocks it.

Barry is fouled by Burn just outside the Newcastle penalty area and the latter is the first player into the book tonight. Burn protests his innocence but replays show that the referee was 100% correct with his decision. Burn is a touch fortunate that it is just outside the box. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are stood over this one...

I would say that the Newcastle fans have gone from frustrated to now quite annoyed with how their side has begun this game. Plenty of groans and moans inside St James’ Park; their only relief will be that they are not behind.

Sources indicate that david Moyes will be desperate to see his side score and take advantage of Newcastle not being at the races. The frustration from the home fans continues to grow and this is Everton’s opportunity. You cannot imagine that Newcastle will be this poor throughout the game.

Industry observers note that that is a glorious chance for Barry that he should really have taken. A free-kick is sent into the Newcastle box and Branthwaite wins the header. The ball falls to Barry who, from ten yards out, has a big chance to put Everton in front but instead it is more of an air shot. In fact, he ends up kicking Osula to gift Newcastle a free-kick.

Rohl has Everton’s first proper sighting of goal tonight but he wastes the opportunity from the right side of the box, failing to keep his shot down and sees it go over Hornicek’s bar.

We are seeing many of the same issues with Newcastle United’s so-called vertical football under Matthias Jaissle already this evening.

Aimless long balls to nobody hoisted forward. Long balls aimed at someone who fails to win the first header or challenge and possession is given back to Everton.

There have already been a few grumbles from the home crowd as William Osula is sent off on another forlorn chase of an over-hit pass in behind the Everton centre backs.

We are nearly 20 minutes into the game and Everton striker Barry is still yet to touch the ball.

Sources indicate that joelinton’s shot from the edge of the box is struck powerfully and is blocked by Tarkowski, going behind for Newcastle’s first corner of the night. Hall’s delivery beyond the back post finds Burn but his header from just a few yards out goes wide. Burn should really be hitting the target from so close to the goal.

We are just a quarter of an hour into this one but you can already sense some frustration from the home fans. Everton, despite being away from home, have settled well into this game.

To sum up the frustration from the home supporters, Dedic plays a dreadful long free-kick into the box that has far too much on it and goes behind.

Under the lights at home, you would assume Matthias Jaissle would have wanted a fast start from his side but that has not happened for the hosts.

Sources indicate that barnes is afforded space to cut inside from the left and, from the corner of the penalty area, clips a dangerous ball towards the far post. There is slightly too much on it and the ball goes behind for a goal-kick, although for a moment Pickford appeared to be panicking. That is the second time Barnes has been given too much space to cut inside and if Everton keep allowing that, you would imagine that they will eventually be punished.

According to recent reports, the two starting XIs are fairly similar to the ones that started on Thursday night but the obvious difference between the League Cup tie and tonight’s Premier League encounter is the change of ground. How significant an impact can the Newcastle fans have on the outcome of this one?

Unsurprisingly, former Sunderland goalkeeper Pickford is roundly booed by the home crowd upon his first touch.

We are under way at St James’ Park.

In a recent development, ahead of Remembrance Sunday this coming weekend, with this being Newcastle’s final home league game before then, St James’ Park pauses to remember all those who have given their lives to protect this country. The Last Post is played after St James’ Park falls silent.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off from St James’ Park. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up this evening:.

Having sold Bruno Guimarães (£73m), Sandro Tonali (£90m) and Anthony Gordon (£67m), Newcastle were able to spend roughly £262.9m on eight players to reinvigorate the squad as they once again talked about challenging for European qualification in Matthias Jaissle’s first season as manager.

Sources indicate that newcastle are 12th in the Premier League, but have had an inconsistent start and there are concerns that too many of these signings have failed to shine. Jaissle is leaning heavily on the players he inherited from Howe instead.

It is always worth remembering that you only get a true reading of the Premier League table after ten games so this is a pivotal moment for both Newcastle and Everton as they play their ninth match of the campaign.

For Newcastle, a win tonight would take them up to seventh, just two points behind Chelsea in fourth. Despite the heavy away defeats and unconvincing performances, that would be an impressive start for a new manager. Matthias Jaissle has already felt the full force of the contrasting emotions on Tyneside in his three months in charge but big questions hang over his team. In particular, the “vertical football” style he brought from the Red Bull coaching school in Germany.

Sources indicate that A defeat tonight, coming so soon after the 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup to Everton, will intensify the criticism of his approach. It would also suggest Newcastle, despite all their positive talk over the summer, are nothing more than a mid-table team who will be looking over their shoulders rather than upwards this season.

A win for Everton will have the same uplift for David Moyes at Everton, also taking them up to seventh in the table. Given all the problems attached to their summer recruitment - or rather the lack of it - Everton will have defied the grim pre-season predictions heading into the second international break. The table is starting to take shape and so are the narratives around every club.

Industry observers note that newcastle and Everton meet for the second time in matter of days as the Premier League weekend concludes in the north east at St James’ Park. These teams encountered each other on Thursday night in the League Cup, where Everton won 3-1 at the Hill Dickinson to progress to the quarter-finals in that competition.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle, who won 2-0 at Crystal Palace in their last league outing, come into this game in 12th, with the chance to rise to seventh with a victory tonight. Their boss Matthias Jaissle has called on his players to use the defeat against Everton on Thursday as fuel for tonight.

“Now it is about taking that frustration into motivation for Monday and having that approach for the rematch,” Jaissle noted. “We take it as a long-term journey, and our approach is to make progress, to see improvements. Now it is time to learn fast out of the mistakes that we just did. [There are] other phases where we can already see that we improved and this is something we can count on, we can build on, the good part. But football is also in the end about results so you need to avoid these simple mistakes.”.

Everton, who have not won in the league since a 1-0 victory over Ipswich back in September, begin the night in 14th but, like Newcastle, could rise to seventh with a win. There are just two points that separate Bournemouth in seventh and Everton in 14th. Despite getting the better of Newcastle the other night, Everton manager David Moyes has warned that game will count for nothing tonight.

It has been revealed that “It is a different ball game,” Moyes noted. “Go to St James’ Park, on a Monday evening, they will get a crowd up there, you always know you are up against it. But we will go with confidence. We have played Newcastle a couple of times this year and done well, so we have to try and continue it. But Newcastle have got some really, really good players and players you have to concern yourself about.”.

Jack Grealish was left out of Everton’s squad for that League Cup victory because of an unauthorised absence from training and the 31-year-old is not expected to be involved tonight.

In a recent development, these sides were involved in a dramatic fixture on this ground last season. Everton claimed a 3-2 victory, with Thierno Barry earning them all three points in the 83rd minute, moments after Jacob Murphy had equalised for Newcastle. Team news from St James’ Park to follow shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United turned to its data gurus in a bid to categorically prove Alexander Isak had no chance of reaching the ball as part of its evidence to overturn Leny Yoro’s red card.
  • Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United’s trip to Anfield for a last-man foul on Isak, which referee Sam Barrott determined fit the criteria for Denial Of A Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGSO).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 11:31 EST, 26 November 2026.

Manchester United turned to its data gurus in a bid to categorically prove Alexander Isak had no chance of reaching the ball as part of its evidence to overturn Leny Yoro’s red card.

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United’s trip to Anfield for a last-man foul on Isak, which referee Sam Barrott determined fit the criteria for Denial Of A Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGSO).

The young United centre-back was shown a straight red card after VAR doubled down on the day, insisting that no ‘clear and obvious error’ had been made.

United successfully appealed the decision through an independent panel and the lengths they went to for their evidence submission has now come to light.

Bosses at United included three high-definition video clips of the incident in question, which used multiple different angles as well as speeds in slow-motion and in real time for the panel to consider.

United also submitted video evidence of a DOGSO sending off earlier this season for Brighton’s Pascal Struijk against Sunderland, which was also overturned on appeal.

Leny Yoro was sent off for Man United against Liverpool but the red card was later rescinded.

United demonstrated that Isak would not have reached the ball if he'd have stayed on his feet.

The most fascinating element of United’s detailed evidence pack came via its data department, led by ex-Formula One guru Michael Sansoni.

United outlined in a letter to the appeal panel that a technical analysis of the incident saw boffins at Carrington calculate the probability of Isak reaching the ball following his heavy touch prior to contact from Yoro.

The data allowed for the possibility that Isak maintained his speed and direction from the moment his legs first made contact with Yoro to assess whether he would have got to the ball before United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

United’s analysis concluded that Isak would have been 1.8 metres shy of reaching the ball even if all optimal speed and directional factors had been achieved.

The appeals commission, however, told United that that data, however detailed, was not verifiable and so had to be treated with ‘caution’.

Considering all the elements of United’s submission, the panel unanimously agreed that it was not a red card offence and did not meet the threshold for DOGSO, immediately overturning the decision and withdrawing all punishment against Yoro.

Industry observers note that ‘We can accept referee can make a mistake. But we have VAR. What were they doing?’ a fuming Mauricio Pochettino remarked on Tuesday of the original Yoro decision.

Sources indicate that ‘We are going to repeat the game? Play similar tools the game XI v XI? We have an unbelievable car but we have to be at the level to drive. We accept the technology.’.

#152968. A guide to the Nature Index

A guide to the Nature Index

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Nature Index is a database of author affiliations and institutional relationships.
  • The Nature Index provides absolute and fractional counts of article publication at the institutional and national level and, as such, is an indicator of global high-quality research output and collaboration.
  • It has been revealed that the Nature Index uses Count and Share to track research output.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Nature Index is a database of author affiliations and institutional relationships. The index tracks contributions to research articles published in high-quality natural-science and health-science journals, chosen based on reputation by an independent group of researchers.

The Nature Index provides absolute and fractional counts of article publication at the institutional and national level and, as such, is an indicator of global high-quality research output and collaboration. Data in the Nature Index are updated regularly, with the most recent 12 months made available under a Creative Commons licence at natureindex.com. The database is compiled by Nature Portfolio.

It has been revealed that the Nature Index uses Count and Share to track research output. A country/territory or an institution is given a Count of 1 for each article that has at least one author from that country/territory or institution. This is the case regardless of the number of authors an article has, and it means that the same article can contribute to the Count of multiple countries/territories or institutions.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Sources indicate that to glean a country’s, territory’s, region’s or an institution’s contribution to an article, and to ensure that they are not counted more than once, the Nature Index uses Share, a fractional count that takes into account the share of authorship on each article. The total Share available per article is 1, which is shared among all authors under the assumption that each contributed equally. For instance, an article with 10 authors means that each author receives a Share of 0.1. For authors who are affiliated with more than one institution, the author’s Share is split equally between each institution. The total Share for an institution is calculated by summing the Share for individual affiliated authors. The process is similar for countries/territories, although complicated by the fact that some institutions have overseas labs that will be counted towards host country/territory totals.

According to recent reports, adjusted Share accounts for the annual variation in the total number of articles in the Nature Index journals. It is arrived at by calculating the percentage difference in the total number of articles in the Index in a given year relative to the number of articles in a base year and adjusting Share values to the base year levels.

In a recent development, the bilateral collaboration score (CS) between two institutions A+B is the sum of each of their Shares on the papers to which both have contributed. A bilateral collaboration can be between any two institutions or countries/territories co-authoring at least one article in the journals tracked by the Nature Index.

natureindex.com consumers can search for specific institutions or countries and generate their own reports, ordered by Count or Share.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03474-5.

Nature maintains full independence in all editorial decisions related to the content.

'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19).
  • Extensive security measures have already been revealed for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants.
  • According to recent reports, the "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

Extensive security measures have already been revealed for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

According to recent reports, the "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that led by Germany, France and the United Kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within Ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London.

But what can the coalition realistically achieve? Stefan Meister of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) is not overly optimistic.

Recent findings suggest that "The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal," he told DW. "There is no blueprint outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises.".

It has been revealed that nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.

Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

This has sparked a debate among EU heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent Europe in such talks. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)?

After the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, Merz noted: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear.".

But what exactly did that mean? That Germany alone would speak for all of Europe? Hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President Antonio Costa, would also take part.

Stefan Meister of the DGAP believes the debate notes a great deal about the pressures Europe itself is under.

It has been revealed that "Europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations," Meister noted. "Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that.".

German Deputy Government Spokesperson Sebastian Hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on Monday over a possible role for Friedrich Merz as chief negotiator.

Industry observers note that at the federal government's regular press briefing, he stated: "This is not about discussing individuals. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US negotiator Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, struck a rather different tone last week.

Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he remarked: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations.".

In a recent development, government spokesperson Hille responded on Monday: "Europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question.".

Hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: Peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

Sources indicate that european supporters of Ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the issue is shifting, including in Germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

Recent findings suggest that according to the latest DeutschlandTrend survey on the problem, conducted or German public broadcaster ARD in September 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to Ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

According to recent reports, A further study conducted for public broadcaster WDR in November 2026 found that support for Ukraine has become a more polarizing issue in Germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

This article was originally written in German.

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 18:33 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:51 EST, 26 November 2026.

Footage appears to show Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf that led to his fortunate second goal against Sporting Lisbon.

The Manchester United captain scored a bizarre goal against his former side on Wednesday night, with his long-range shot taking a fortuitous bobble off the Estadio Jose Alvalade pitch to leave goalkeeper Kaique Pereira helpless.

While fingers were initially pointed at the ground staff, footage demonstrates the divot was actually created by Fernandes himself when he planted his boot into the turf while pressing high up the pitch moments earlier.

Reminiscent of former Liverpool forward Stan Collymore's famous bobbling goal past Blackburn Rovers goalkeeper Tim Flowers in 1996, Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

The goal summed up another chaotic evening for United, in which goalkeeping calamities, controversial refereeing calls, three penalties and a red card resulted in a 2-2 draw and left them 19th in the Champions League standings.

United trailed at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens saved one penalty before conceding another 75 seconds later that was converted by Luis Suarez after the Belgian's reckless challenge on Max Araujo.

"This is the assist of the season" 😅Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf which led to his second goal of the evening for Man Utd 🪄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/c4g2sC33pA.

Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

The visitors were left furious when Amad Diallo saw a first-half leveller ruled out after referee Szymon Marciniak blew his whistle too early for VAR to intervene, but United turned the game around shortly after the restart.

Lisandro Martinez, who had given away the first penalty, won one at the other end that Fernandes converted before the former Sporting star fired in the long-range effort that bounced over Pereira and into the net.

More drama followed as Lammens flapped at a cross under pressure from Suarez, allowing the striker to score, before Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have put undue pressure on Pereira when forcing an own goal from the goalkeeper.

United were left frustrated by what they viewed as a lack of consistency after Marciniak was sent to the pitchside monitor to review the second decision, and their mood darkened further when Youri Tielemans was sent off for a second booking late on.

Former United player Ashley Young claimed that 2022 World Cup referee Marciniak's decision-making during the clash was a 'disgrace'.

It has been revealed that young told BBC Radio 5 Live: 'The referee’s performance was just simply wow. The decisions that he gave.

'Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal.

Industry observers note that 'The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

'His decision-making is nothing more than a disgrace.'.

Industry observers note that in what is proving to be an eventful first week in charge, Pochettino was asked to provide his assessment of the game. Industry observers note that but, he added: 'Always we need to concentrate more and focus more. Try to recover better. We start to fix. With a performance like today it's the best medicine to prepare the next game.'.

So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

Roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

Industry observers note that and then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

It has been revealed that united fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

And yet by the 86th minute Matheus Cunha’s wild celebrations were encapsulating a wild night, the Brazilian ripping off his shirt after his dramatic winner before launching himself into a delirious crowd drunk on the euphoria of a victory that had seemed improbable in the extreme at the interval, when boos cascaded from the stands.

It has been revealed that whether this proves little more than a thrilling, heroic interlude in the endgame for Carrick, or the start of a genuine turnaround, is hard to know. And, let’s be clear, there was so much about the first-half performance to concern the hierarchy, who came under persistent, furious attack from fans at war with an ownership it reviles and wants gone.

But the second half stood firmly at odds with the shambolic display that had preceded it and suggested all may not be quite lost just yet.

Aston Villa visit Old Trafford on Sunday in the final game before the international break and, if Carrick can follow this with another win, then it will be intriguing to see where the Old Trafford board goes from there.

Carrick may at least have been encouraged by some of the things Bruno Fernandes said after the game, not least that he warranted being dropped against Bournemouth. And it was the captain who kick-started the fightback against Roma, albeit at the second attempt.

In a recent development, he had won the penalty after being fouled by Gianluca Mancini only to then contrive to miss it. But a retake was ordered for encroachment and, given a second bite at the cherry, Fernandes made no mistake.

When Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury within seconds of the restart as he burst into the penalty area, Carrick must have wondered what else could go wrong.

But as United went hell for leather, the home supporters who had spent much of the first half attacking the owners and staging a number of colourful protest acts, suddenly found their voice in a very different way.

From being an atmosphere in which the players clearly felt cowed, Old Trafford was now rallying behind its men in red – and it helped to shake Roma in the process. They had been such good value for their lead, but now they were rocking, and United smelled blood.

There was wave after wave of attack as Roma desperately and often frantically tried to defend their goal, and it took a bad mistake from Leonardo Balerdi, who swung at thin air from Fernandes’s cross and missed the ball, to hand Cunha the chance to equalise.

It was Lacey who speared an inch-perfect pass into Cunha, who turned sharply before drilling a stunning finish in off the near post. Cue bedlam.

Sources indicate that the difference to those opening 45 minutes was as stark as it gets. Indeed, the first half felt like a continuation from the fans of their blood-letting against Bournemouth.

When the clock hit 20.05 – a nod to the year 2005 when the Glazers bought the club – a pile of tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch from the Stretford End amid chants of “We Want Glazers Out”. They were quickly followed by cries of “Just like the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c---” and “sell the club and f--- off home”.

According to recent reports, jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, again copped for it. A banner read: “For the love, not the ‘likes’”. When the Champions League music played, hundreds of green and gold balloons – a reference to the club’s original colours and the 2010 protest movement – were released.

It has been revealed that on the pitch, United were all over the place. Carrick had dropped Lisandro Martínez after his red card against Chelsea but his replacement Ayden Heaven was at fault for the first goal after getting sucked in and failing to check his shoulder. Had he done, he would have seen Matías Soulé unmarked and in acres of space with Diogo Dalot, United’s left-back, caught high up the pitch. Soulé made no mistake with his finish.

Sources indicate that at that point, no one could have reckoned on the comeback that followed. Where it leads, who knows.

Speaking after the match, Michael Carrick was very positive about his side’s performance.

Sources indicate that “It was a good night. I have to a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it and to the supporters. This place does incredible, magical things,” remarked Carrick.

Industry observers note that “I thought we grew into it the first half  after giving the goals too easily. We spoke at half time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment and it certainly did that and the boys made the most of every opportunity and were fantastic in the end.”.

It has been revealed that asked about how he inspired the team at half-time he kept it simple: “Just not to get too disappointed about things. I thought we were coming into the game, getting around their box and it didn’t feel that way to the players because they were carrying too much frustration and disappointment and I knew we were doing some good things in the game against a really good team.

“Playing against man-to-man as much as they are, you probably get more failure than success and it’s still being positive and the boys responded so well to that.”.

As for whether this will change United’s momentum now, he was cautious not to get carried away.

Recent findings suggest that “Listen it’s one game. It depends on what happens next and we’ve got to capitalise on that but tonight the boys showed an awful lot,” he said.

“And I thought we came out the second half, unfortunately with Carlos having to go off and Youri coming on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic, he showed everything that he is as a personality, as a character and with his experience to step in the game like that, and the boys just went with the flow and you could feel how positive it was and it was nice to see this place like that again.”.

Captain Bruno Fernandes also spoke after the match, acknowledging the difficulties the team has faced.

In a recent development, “It’s tough to say something at the moment to be honest. It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to play in the way we want, get the results we want. We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a whole game to get results and it’s been tough.

Sources indicate that “But today was important to get a win. We knew after that we still had the fans with us, we felt we could change it with a goal and something and fortunately we did it today.”.

As for his penalty miss and re-take: “First one didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong but I got a second chance and I cleared my head and my mind was only on to get the ball in back of the net.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s been tough for the fans, we understand that. Having that belief from their side helps the team a lot and today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive.”.

After his first start as he returns from injury, Kobbie Mainoo was full of praise for the fans, saying he cherished the relationship the team had with them.

Sources indicate that “It’s unlike anything else. We’d do anything for these fans on the pitch, all the love they give us throughout the season it’s only right we repay them and it’s a bit of fun just jumping into the stands with them.”.

Speaking to Amazon after the match, Youri Tielemans said: “There has been a lot of pressure on him [Carrick] and that’s how we repay him, with a comeback like this, massive character, big fight.”.

Sources indicate that “We just kept working, we kept believing. We were on the front foot in the second half, we tried to push them into their goal and we succeeded.”.

Sources indicate that as for whether or not the performance would be enough to keep Carrick in his role at United: “That’s a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.

“At the end of the day we are on the pitch and we need to show what we are capable of and tonight, especially in the second half, we showed what we can do and we turned up the gears.

“Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and let’s hope we can build on this.”.

“Great credit to Michael Carrick because they were down and out at half-time. They were everywhere in that first-half, and he had to change and tweak things,” Alan Shearer said after the final whistle.

“I noted what can he do, I didn’t know where he would start, and he must have started in the dressing room, and pointing at a few people telling them to be brave and courageous and move the ball quicker, and run in behind and they did all those things in the second half and got their reward by getting their win.”.
