💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
  • Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era.
  • During his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

During his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

At the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

Recent findings suggest that infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is said to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment initiative, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

According to recent reports, however, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

Sources indicate that philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf noted in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

It has been revealed that "We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction.".

Recent findings suggest that diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

The third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he mentioned.

Sources indicate that "Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization.".

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

Recent findings suggest that but he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo said he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he said.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

How Leeds United turned into Champions League contenders: Insiders reveal the ways 'manager's dream' Ethan Ampadu drives standards on and off the pitch, a hidden tougher side to Daniel Farke - and the club's January transfer window strategy

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:04 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 10:46 EST, 27 November 2026.
  • He may not realise it yet, but the key member of Leeds United’s ever-improving team might just become one of their next great managers.
  • Leeds have been deservedly praised for their impressive start to the season, which sees them a point away from the likely Champions League places ahead of Saturday’s clash with Coventry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:04 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 10:46 EST, 27 November 2026.

He may not realise it yet, but the key member of Leeds United’s ever-improving team might just become one of their next great managers.

Leeds have been deservedly praised for their impressive start to the season, which sees them a point away from the likely Champions League places ahead of Saturday’s clash with Coventry.

Boss Daniel Farke is re-establishing the club in the top flight. Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a upcoming contract and is an England player again. Towering centre back Tarik Muharemovic looks the buy of the season. The 49ers Enterprises Group are shrewd and careful owners.

It has been revealed that but what about the guy who knits it all together? Ethan Ampadu had played for six clubs in three countries before he joined Leeds in 2023 but now he has found his home. Nearly half of Ampadu’s senior appearances have been in a Leeds shirt.

Ampadu’s work on the pitch and his behaviour off it suggest a manager in the making. Team-mates turn to him instinctively during matches and off the field, too, he makes Leeds tick.

‘I don’t know what Ethan’s prepares are when he's finished playing but he has the stature and could offer a lot to the game beyond his playing career,’ claims Stuart Dallas, who helped Leeds return to the Premier League in 2020 during an outstanding nine-year career at Elland Road.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at why Leeds are on the rise – starting with their inspirational captain.

Inspired by brilliant new signings including Tarik Muharemovic (left) and James Trafford, Leeds are on the rise and in contention for the Champions League spots.

Captain Ethan Ampadu makes Leeds tick on and off the pitch and is perceived as a manager in waiting.

In the here and now, boss Daniel Farke is doing a superb job, having narrowly avoided being sacked in previous seasons.

Though Dallas retired due to injury at the end of Ampadu’s first campaign at Leeds, he liked what he saw in those months.

‘I was at the training ground recently and the players had a later start – they were preparing for a Sunday game,’ Dallas, now a regular television pundit, tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘He was the first to turn up for the session. If you’re a young player coming through, it’s fantastic to see the captain setting that example.

‘He is an intelligent guy who takes responsibility. In his position you have to front up when things are not going well and protect people when they need it. He understands that.

‘A manager doesn’t want 20 different people knocking on his door. Ethan will take a lot of those minor problems away and I know how much of a privilege it is to him to captain Leeds.’.

Ampadu takes the role extremely seriously. Daily Mail Sport understands he ensured Under-21 players who train regularly with the first team were included in the players' bonus pool. He also made sure they were listed as first-team squad members on the club website.

Ampadu wants the squad to feel like a family and will organise team bonding trips and meals out. Little things like that go a heck of a long way.

The club's leadership group comprises Ampadu, Calvert-Lewin, Jaka Bijol, Joe Rodon and James Justin – but third-choice goalkeeper Alex Cairns is another hugely respected figure in the squad.

Prolific striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin (pictured scoring in Leeds' 4-1 rout of Chelsea last weekend) has signed a fresh contract with the club.

Calvert-Lewin (with Noah Okafor, right) is part of the team's leadership group, led by Ampadu.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Ethan is a manager’s dream,’ explains former Leeds boss Simon Grayson, now a regular pundit on Leeds’ in-house TV channel LUTV. ‘Someone like that makes the manager’s job much less stressful.

Sources indicate that ‘If there’s an incident on or off the pitch, sometimes the captain can deal with it before it reaches the manager’s door. Ethan will do that. He has a level of respect from the other players so if he says something, it’s no different from Daniel Farke saying it.’.

Farke is usually cautious when bringing back players from injury. When they are as important as Ampadu, though, he is prepared to make an exception.

Sources indicate that the 26-year-old does not immediately catch the eye. He does not make spectacular passes or beat three opponents with a piece of skill. He has only three goals in 139 appearances.

Instead, he steps back into defence to cover the forward runs of Justin or Jayden Bogle. He makes sure he is in the right spot to stop counter-attacks. He is the one to notice when a team-mate has drifted out of position when defending a set-piece. Scouts see this and this is why Ampadu was considered by clubs in the so-called ‘Massive Six’ before he signed a new four-year deal with Leeds last June.

In a recent development, ‘He’ll go in and smash someone – fairly – if it’s a quiet game because it will wake the crowd up a bit,’ smiles Grayson. ‘You only realise how much you miss players like that when they are not in the team.’.

Industry observers note that ampadu is just as popular with the fans. ‘As Leeds captains go, Gary McAllister and Lucas Radebe set a high bar when I was growing up,' indicates Rocco Dean of the Leeds, That! podcast. 'Although Ampadu has a little way to go, it's not inconceivable he could one day rank alongside those greats.'.

Industry observers note that at any time, there will usually be two or three players in a squad who are not popular with supporters. It is difficult to find them in the current Leeds side. ‘The players want to play for Leeds and it’s not just a "job",’ adds Mike Chard, who runs the All Leeds TV YouTube channel. ‘They don’t seem like a team. They seem like a family.’.

Sources indicate that ‘As Leeds captains go, Gary McAllister and Lucas Radebe set a high bar when I was growing up... but Ampadu could one day rank alongside those greats'.

Leeds have a broad agreement with Farke over a upcoming contract and he deserves it. If Leeds beat Coventry, it will be his 80th win as boss in 162 games. Bielsa reached 80 in 163 matches.

In front of the cameras, Farke is open and affable – but he is no soft touch with his squad or coaches. The staff member who wore a snood over his head to training this week will be forced to don shorts and T-shirt for the remainder of the winter. His crime? Acting ‘significant time’.

Footballers like to fool about when they are together but few would dare risk it when Farke is nearby. Daily Mail Sport has heard of one player who was acting the goat in the canteen and turned white when he realised he had failed to notice Farke entering the room.

According to recent reports, some bosses will encourage players to ask why they have been left out of the team. That is not typically the case with Farke. Generally, he makes his choices and then it falls to players to prove him wrong through their displays in training.

According to recent reports, he can still forge close relationships with players, though. His rapport with Calvert-Lewin was a factor in the striker’s new deal and he has a similarly strong understanding with Noah Okafor.

Farke is probably as powerful now as he has ever been during his three-and-a-half seasons at Elland Road. At different points during his two Championship campaigns in charge, Farke was vulnerable to the sack. Even early last season, things looked a little dicey for him.

Switching to a back three in the 3-2 defeat at Manchester City last November turned it around for Leeds but this is about much more than a simple change of formation.

Despite his affable exterior and close bonds with certain players, Farke has a disciplinarian streak.

Industry observers note that most of Leeds’ medical and conditioning team have been at Elland Road for more than a decade and unlike at many clubs, there is complete trust between them and Farke. The result? No injuries to first-team players as things stand.

Recent findings suggest that on their instruction, Farke restricted Okafor to a 20-minute substitute appearance against Tottenham earlier this month. The Swiss attacker still scored the only goal.

It has been revealed that in a typical week after a Saturday game, players will report to Thorp Arch for a recovery session on Sunday and have Monday off. Wednesday is usually the toughest day – gym in the morning followed by a training session, and more gym work in the afternoon.

Farke and his staff favour two particular possession drills: a four-a-side game with three ‘floating’ players who work with whoever has the ball, and a 10-a-side exercise with two floating players.

In a recent development, brighton and Brentford have set the standard for recruitment in the last decade yet since promotion Leeds have not been far behind. Chairman Paraag Marathe has worked for global management consultants Bain, who rely heavily on data.

According to recent reports, led by sporting director Adam Underwood, Leeds do the same – though they mix art with science. New signings are shown videos of the celebrations in the city when Leeds were promoted in 2025. The current brief is to find physically robust, athletic players and unlike many clubs, Leeds are not obsessed with youth. The average age of their starting XI for the 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge was 27 years and 107 days. That figure has not dipped below 26 in any league game this season.

Underwood and his team anticipate a quiet January window in which no key players are expected to leave – dashing any hopes rivals may have had of stealing Muharemovic. The defender joined from Sassuolo for £30.1million last summer and his value is already much higher.

Recent findings suggest that under chairman Paraag Marathe (right), Leeds rely heavily on data in their recruitment. Their transfer track record has been excellent in recent years.

According to recent reports, the pinch point for the 49ers is coming. They aim to make Leeds worth £1billion by 2030. That will require significantly greater revenue: in 2024-25, when Leeds were promoted from the Championship, their revenue was £137m. That was a record for the second tier but they will likely need to exceed £300m in the coming years to hit the 49ers' £1bn target.

According to recent reports, an expanded Elland Road should plug some of this gap when work is complete. Leeds are working on each stand in turn and hope the project will be finished by the end of 2030, giving them a 53,000 capacity.

Earlier this month, Leeds instructed US bank Allen & Co to seek additional investment, though it is thought a full sale is not at the moment on the cards.

Industry observers note that christian Purslow offers a different perspective. The former Aston Villa CEO, who also held senior positions at Liverpool and Chelsea, knows how tough it is for clubs outside the Big Six to break into that wealthy elite.

Industry observers note that speaking on The Football Boardcast, Purslow stated: ‘If I were Paraag Marathe, I’d be looking at what’s gone on at some of my natural peers – Newcastle, Aston Villa, West Ham, Leicester, Everton. It’s so precarious when clubs like these try hard to push up against the so-called Big Six.

‘These guys (the 49ers) might conclude: "We’ve done our job, we’ve enjoyed the journey, let’s let someone else have the problem of competing with the Big Six in a world where Premier League and UEFA financial rules make it increasingly difficult." I would not rule that out in the next couple of years.’.

Industry News: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that another crucial opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control.
  • A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
  • Industry observers note that A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that another crucial opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last big media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Industry observers note that A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

Sources indicate that the broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a new account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

The Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

Sources indicate that according to the investigators, Akbay is said to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

Recent findings suggest that it is not latest for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

Industry observers note that sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

Sources indicate that in the space of just over a year, three of the most important opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

In a recent development, esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen claims Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

Recent findings suggest that esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he states, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

Sources indicate that several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that the Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and revealed its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, showed how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it mentioned.

In a recent development, "These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

This article has been translated from German.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy.
  • The significant talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area.
  • According to recent reports, “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy. Mikel Arteta’s instant simmering fury at being denied a first-half penalty may also have turned into something rather more explosive had Martin Odegaard not later sent the champions six points clear with a ninth win in 10 Premier League games.

The significant talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area. Which came first? The intervention of VAR suggested the latter. But Hallam duly went to check the pitch-side monitor before then announcing the former.

According to recent reports, “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared. Cue cheers from the home Arsenal crowd. “However…,” he went on. “Red No 29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City.”.

#ARSHUL – 42' VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. REF: "After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No.32 on Red No.29. However, Red No.29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City".

Industry observers note that it all sounded so decisive that most inside the Emirates instinctively thought the outcome reasonable. But then came a closer look at the rules. And Law 11.2 certainly did seem to support Arteta’s protestations: “In situations where a player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

Recent findings suggest that arteta clearly saw no value after the match in aiming much criticism at Hallam following a fourth 1-0 win in 10 league games, but did still emphasise his surprise at the decision. “What do you think?” he asked one reporter. “I thought offside, but the law states that doesn’t matter,” replied the journalist. “So not offside then,” mentioned Arteta, who stressed that he needs to understand “what is overruling what in the decision-making” after a Premier League statement simply said that Havertz was deemed offside “in the build-up”.

In a recent development, at the very best, it all leaves further confusion and again opens refereeing body Pro Ref to the charge of inconsistency. Fabian Schär, for example, was awarded a penalty for Newcastle against Bournemouth in 2024, despite being in an offside position when his shirt was grabbed by Adam Smith.

In a recent development, conversely, Dango Ouattara had a penalty overturned for Brentford against Leeds last season after going down under pressure from Gabriel Gudmundsson before being deemed offside. The crucial point seems to be whether the player has actually challenged for the ball at the time of the infringement and, in this case, the answer was surely “no”.

In a recent development, premier League title triumphs, however, are often forged on forgettable wins in frustrating circumstances and this was ultimately a classic of the genre. With Noni Madueke continuing to step up superbly in the absence of Bukayo Saka, Arsenal’s combination of attacking persistence and defensive resilience was ultimately rewarded by Odegaard’s scrappy 72nd-minute shot. For young players, it was also every bit as educational as the VAR controversy might be for emerging officials.

Madueke’s low shot forced a save by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, but Odegaard was somehow first to the rebound, despite being the wrong side of the penalty spot and five yards behind Hull defender John Egan when the ball was struck.

“The way he scores, not the most beautiful, but the most effective,” said Arteta, who said that his team had sometimes tried too hard for a “perfect goal” and should instead be happy with something “more pragmatic”.

It was a well-judged assessment as Arsenal head into the international break with creative deficiencies, but still almost flawless in the cold hard currency of results. Three wins in three days, including at Anfield and in Prague, also underlines a certain champions mentality.

In a recent development, “I need to praise the players,” said Arteta. “It’s been very very demanding; very short time to recover with all the travel. The mentality is incredible. It’s still going to be super difficult. We can improve in a number of areas.”.

When it was then put to him that Arsenal have been offside 35 times this season – with Havertz responsible for 15 of those – Arteta acknowledged that “timing” was one element. But, with Havertz targeted by some frustrated fans, he stressed that responsibility was always shared for those split-second moments by the passer and receiver.

He also singled out Madueke, again easily Arsenal’s most creative player, following his surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad. “He went away, started to train, he came back and it was a different Noni,” mentioned Arteta, of his reaction to also being out of the Arsenal team earlier in the season. “You could sense that he meant business and he wasn’t going to accept the situation and, since then, I think he’s been incredible.”.

An improved showing by Jaissle’s Newcastle, but they will be dissapointed that they failed to see it through after Jacob Murphy scored in the 80th minute.

Industry observers note that arsenal far from their best, but it is another one-goal win in the Premier League. They are now six points clear at the top of the Premier League, and it is 27 points from the first 30 available.

Mikel Arteta has remarked Arsenal are “looking after” Declan Rice more now than in any previous campaign and has rejected suggestions that the England midfielder is being overplayed.

Rice played through nerve pain in his hamstring in the second half of last season, when he made an extraordinary 69 appearances for club and country.

The 27-year-old has played at least 60 matches in each of the past four campaigns, prompting concerns among Arsenal supporters that he is at risk of burnout or injury.

Arteta kept Rice on the field for the full 90 minutes of Arsenal’s midweek victory over Slavia Prague but insisted the club is working harder than ever to manage the midfielder’s workload.

So far this season, Rice has been left out of Arsenal’s two Carabao Cup matches and also withdrew from the previous international break in September.

Asked if he was concerned about Rice’s fitness, Arteta remarked: “Concerns? Which is the only player, the only player in this squad, that for two games in the Carabao Cup has been left out of the squad? At home with two days off? It’s not true [that Rice is being overplayed].

“We are really looking after him more than any other season. The way he is training and all the love [he is being shown]. That’s it.

It has been revealed that “Here are the demands of this football club and a player like him. Not only him, because there are many others that have even less time. That’s it. That has to be the mindset. If you start to put other things in your brain, [it will create] damage. Erase them, get them in the bin and just focus on what you have to do.”.

Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

In a recent development, hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

There is one other three o’clock kick-off: Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage, with Matthias Jaissle under increasing pressure.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. There were reports of dressing room unrest, but Fulham rank highly for possession and chance creation so it appears the Spaniard is putting his stamp on things.

Full team news on the way shortly.

According to recent reports, by harnessing potent antibodies that can vanquish diverse viral strains, scientists are closing in on one of the most elusive goals in biomedical research: a vaccine for HIV. This year, several research teams described vaccination strategies that triggered the production of these broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) in monkeys, and precursors to bnAbs in people, suggesting that an effective vaccine is possible. But devastating cuts to US funding for HIV research have left some efforts in limbo.

Recent findings suggest that the world is closer than it has ever been to an effective HIV vaccine. It also has a drug capable of preventing infections: the long-acting injectable drug lenacapavir, which could avert an estimated one-third of new HIV infections in Africa if given to just 5% of adults. Now is the time for funders to ramp up investment, not cut it back, argues a Nature editorial.

Reference: UNAIDS & Gates Foundation report.

In a recent development, pregnancy causes drastic changes to the brain, but we know little about them because of past worries about the safety of scanning pregnant people. Now, researchers are working to fill that void by collecting scans from first- and second-time mothers and analysing thousands of archived brain scans acquired during routine clinical care. The work, presented last week at the US Society for Neuroscience annual meeting, could help to explain maternal mental-health conditions such as postpartum depression.

‘General purpose’ artificial-intelligence tools such as OpenAI’s GPT and Anthropic’s Claude are impressing researchers with their emerging biology skills, including protein design and structure prediction. In some tests, these models have even outperformed those designed specifically for biology tasks and trained on vast troves of protein-sequence data. Some scientists predict that generalist AI tools could eventually catch up with, or surpass, blockbuster models such as AlphaFold. Others suggest these newly introduced abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data, rather than advanced learning.

Industry observers note that figure 1 | Position verification. a, To check the location of a party called the prover, two verifiers each send a random bit (a challenge), which are timed to reach the location simultaneously. The prover combines the bits and returns the answer. Because no signal travels faster than light, a prompt reply shows that the prover is at the location. b, However, if two adversaries, one near each verifier, copy a challenge and pass it to each other, they can answer in time even though nobody is at the claimed location. c, In Kavuri and colleagues’ scheme1, one verifier generates two entangled photons, keeping one and sending the other to the prover. Both verifiers then transmit classical challenges. The prover uses the challenges to determine how to measure its photon and returns the result, while the first verifier measures the other photon. If the prover’s result arrives in time and the two measurements pass a statistical check (a Bell test), the transmitted photon must have been measured at the claimed location.

“Banks, power grids and satellite-navigation systems all depend on knowing where a request or a signal comes from, yet claims about location are notoriously easy to fake,” notes physicist Davide Bacco. Now researchers have outlined an experiment in which the position of a distant party is certified using quantum entanglement.

Industry observers note that in a, two verifiers send random bits (challenges) timed to reach the claimed location simultaneously. The prover combines them and replies. Because signals cannot travel faster than light, a prompt response verifies the prover’s location. But two adversaries (b) can defeat this test by exchanging the challenges and responding in time. In (c), a verifier also sends one of two entangled photons, which are inexorably linked in a way that can be proven using a statistical check (a Bell test). If the prover’s result arrives inside the time window imposed by the speed of light and the photons pass the Bell test, the prover must be inside the target region. (Nature | 9 min read).

Industry observers note that chemist George Whitesides made landmark contributions to many fields, including patterning surfaces with molecules — a technique that enabled ‘lab on a chip’ diagnostic devices — advances in nanotechnology and more. He prided himself on switching research interests often, telling students, “If somebody else is working on something, don’t work on it.” In traditional chemistry departments, “there’s often a lot of pressure to stay in your lane, and he made it okay not to”, says polymer scientist Joseph DeSimone. “In fact, he made it exciting not to.” Whitesides has died, aged 87.

Read Whitesides’s guide to writing a scientific paper in a special issue of Advanced Materials that celebrated his 65th birthday.

Some mental disorders seem to take different forms in different places, writes mental-illness researcher Alexander Pereira. “Even depression – arguably the most common psychiatric condition in the world – seems to look strikingly different depending on when and where it appears,” he writes — with bodily symptoms, such as fatigue, prevalent in China, and psychological symptoms, such as low self-esteem, more common in the West. Pereira argues that our ability to adapt to our social environment might significantly shape the internal mechanisms of mental health.

Changing location — even just walking through a doorway — can signal to our brains that work is over and it’s time to relax, states cognitive scientist Joan Ongchoco. (BBC Future | 11 min read).

Reference: Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology paper.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a upcoming guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport.
  • Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a new guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport.
  • Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a upcoming guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport. Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters. Disabled sports broadcaster Andy Stevenson hosted the event, with executives from both Level Playing Field and the Equality and Human Rights Commission addressing attendees. Panel discussions also allowed for insight from industry experts and disabled supporters to be shared with officials from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport, the Sports Grounds Safety Authority and governing bodies across a range of sports. Everton officials and members of Everton Disabled Supporters' Association (EDSA) were among representatives of disabled supporter groups, clubs and venues from across the country. Christopher Massam, Accessibility Lead at Everton Football Club, said: "We are truly honoured to host the launch of Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and to bring together so many great minds and voices on what is a vitally notable subject. "As a Club, we have worked closely with Level Playing Field and EDSA for a number of years as part of our efforts to continually appraise and enhance the accessibility provision across all our stadiums and sites. "Accessibility and inclusivity were key factors in the design of Hill Dickinson Stadium and, since its opening, we have continued to learn from feedback and refine our offering to create the best possible experience for all our supporters and visitors. "Hosting an event like today's allows us to share work we are incredibly proud of, but also to strengthen our relationships with key stakeholders, with supporter groups and to continue that learning journey."Chair of Level Playing Field, Tony Taylor, said: “Today marks an important milestone, as we strive to make attending live sport genuinely accessible for all disabled fans. “It has been our pleasure to lead on this project and channel the input from different stakeholders to define a set of standards and outline a roadmap to deliver access and inclusion. “Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition has the potential to make a dramatic difference to the experiences of so many disabled supporters, and it is important that we all come together to realise this opportunity.” Hill Dickinson Stadium, officially opened in August 2025, offers more wheelchair bays than any other English club stadium and accessible viewing platforms located on multiples levels. The stadium is also equipped with a state-of-the-art sensory room, quiet rooms, Changing Places facilities and low-level counters, as well as providing step-free access to all concourse levels. In addition to hosting Premier League matches, the stadium has become an established home for international football, rugby league and rugby union. To learn more about accessibility provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium, click here. Further details about the Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and how to access the guide, can be found at levelplayingfield.org.uk.

Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a new guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport.

Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters.

Disabled sports broadcaster Andy Stevenson hosted the event, with executives from both Level Playing Field and the Equality and Human Rights Commission addressing attendees.

Panel discussions also allowed for insight from industry experts and disabled supporters to be shared with officials from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport, the Sports Grounds Safety Authority and governing bodies across a range of sports.

Everton officials and members of Everton Disabled Supporters' Association (EDSA) were among representatives of disabled supporter groups, clubs and venues from across the country.

Christopher Massam, Accessibility Lead at Everton Football Club, noted: "We are truly honoured to host the launch of Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and to bring together so many great minds and voices on what is a vitally important subject.

"As a Club, we have worked closely with Level Playing Field and EDSA for a number of years as part of our efforts to continually appraise and enhance the accessibility provision across all our stadiums and sites.

"Accessibility and inclusivity were key factors in the design of Hill Dickinson Stadium and, since its opening, we have continued to learn from feedback and refine our offering to create the best possible experience for all our supporters and visitors.

"Hosting an event like today's allows us to share work we are incredibly proud of, but also to strengthen our relationships with key stakeholders, with supporter groups and to continue that learning journey.".

Chair of Level Playing Field, Tony Taylor, said: “Today marks an important milestone, as we strive to make attending live sport genuinely accessible for all disabled fans.

“It has been our pleasure to lead on this project and channel the input from different stakeholders to define a set of standards and outline a roadmap to deliver access and inclusion.

“Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition has the potential to make a dramatic difference to the experiences of so many disabled supporters, and it is important that we all come together to realise this opportunity.”.

Hill Dickinson Stadium, officially opened in August 2025, offers more wheelchair bays than any other English club stadium and accessible viewing platforms located on multiples levels.

The stadium is also equipped with a state-of-the-art sensory room, quiet rooms, Changing Places facilities and low-level counters, as well as providing step-free access to all concourse levels.

In addition to hosting Premier League matches, the stadium has become an established home for international football, rugby league and rugby union.

To learn more about accessibility provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium, click here.

Further details about the Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and how to access the guide, can be found at levelplayingfield.org.uk.

  • The legendary defender won the Ballon d’Or 20 years ago today.
  • It has been revealed that “Now it’s worth three times more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy legend Fabio Cannavaro admits Zinedine Zidane’s headbutt in the 2006 World Cup Final helped him win the Ballon d’Or: ‘It’s worth three times more now; I don’t see how a defender can win it again.’.

The legendary defender won the Ballon d’Or 20 years ago today. Cannavaro, presently the Uzbekistan national team coach, remains the last defender and the last Italian player to have won the coveted award.

It has been revealed that “Now it’s worth three times more. No defender has won it since, and I don’t see how it can happen again,” he told Gazzetta.

When the journalist argued that Pau Cubarsì might be the closest, Cannavaro replied.

“A Barcelona defender—the city that criticised my victory the most.”.

Catalan newspapers strongly criticised Cannavaro’s Ballon d’Or win 20 years ago, arguing that Barcelona striker Samuel Eto’o deserved it more.

“Criticism has never annoyed me. Now I smile. It seems that it is my fault if Maldini, Baresi or Cubarsì have never won it,” Cannavaro replied.

The former defender revealed how he learned he had won the Ballon d’Or.

“I remember a France Football journalist stopped me in front of the Real Madrid training centre. He got into my car and said: ‘I must tell you something: Buffon can’t reach you; you have won, and we must do an interview.’ I thought: ‘Is this a joke?’ When I watch games of that season, I think: ‘Mamma mia! I was playing so well.’ But I knew, as I know today, that if Zidane had not given that headbutt, it would have been much more complicated.”.

Cannavaro was named the best player in the world in 2006 after helping Italy win the World Cup that year.

The Final against France was one of the most epic games ever and saw Zidane sent off in extra time for headbutting Italy defender Marco Materazzi.

According to recent reports, that Final remains Italy’s last World Cup knockout game. What should Italian football do, especially defensively, to return to greatness?

“We’ve only stopped working on individual technique, on running, and on the habit of defending with the ball frontally and laterally,” Cannavaro replied.

Industry observers note that “Each role has its characteristics, and sometimes they prefer a goalkeeper who can make a 70-meter pass to one who actually makes saves. It’s okay, but then don’t complain if he concedes at an important moment.”.

It has been revealed that when asked whether his mentality has changed now that he has become a coach, Cannavaro replied: “For sure. When you start a coaching career, you think your ideas are the most notable in the world; then you understand you have to adapt. I’ve seen coaches sacked because they wanted to change the team’s menu or train in the morning instead of the afternoon. Let’s say that I’ve become wiser and more experienced.”.

During the same interview, the former Juventus, Napoli, Parma and Inter defender mentioned Liverpool defender Virgil Van Dijk told him during the 2026 World Cup that he’d like to play in Serie A one day.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:49 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 27 November 2026.

Gary Neville has claimed he is 'absolutely certain' Erling Haaland will leave Manchester City for Real Madrid within the next 18 months amid the impact of their legal battle with the Premier League.

Haaland has cut a despondent figure in recent weeks following Man City's underwhelming run of form.

The Norwegian star admitted to 'questioning everything' after their 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League in midweek, while Man City fans expressed concerns over Haaland's downbeat assessment and body language.

The result meant City have won just twice in their last seven matches – one of which was achieved in a penalty shoot-out against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

Man City have suffered defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League in the run, as well as drawing with Fulham on the weekend.

Neville, speaking on the Overlap, suggested the mood at Man City may have been affected in recent weeks after the club were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing. Man City have since appealed the decision.

Gary Neville has noted he is 'absolutely certain' Erling Haaland will leave Manchester City for Real Madrid within the next 18 months.

Neville suggested Haaland's spell at Man City could be coming to an end after questioning whether the 'cloud' of the Premier League charges verdict has impacted the mood at the club.

The former Man United defender theorised that Haaland's time at the club could be coming to an end and that he expects the forward to join Real Madrid in the near future.

'It feels like something has changed in these last few weeks with City, it feels like maybe that mood, that cloud, is just starting to [impact],' Neville said.

'I don't think Haaland is going to be here, I think he will be at Real Madrid in the next, maximum 18 months, maybe even at the end of the season.

'I can see Vinicius leaving, I can see Mbappe going a bit to the left and Haaland going up there [down the middle].

'If you look at Florentino Perez, he goes and signs the best strikers in the world, the best players in the world.

'I just think because of what has happened to City, I think Haaland is going to Real Madrid.

'I am absolutely certain he will be in a Real Madrid shirt in the next 18 months.'.

It had long been viewed that Haaland's career blueprint had involved moving to LaLiga, with Real Madrid long-term admirers.

Real Madrid have held a long-standing interest in the Manchester City superstar.

Neville claimed Real Madrid president Florentino Perez could opt to sell Vinicius Jr before moving for Haaland.

The forward, however, signed a nine-and-a-half-year deal in early 2025, taking his Man City contract through to 2034.

Haaland had pushed back against suggestions the case had affected their form during the international break, while stressing he was committed long-term to the club.

The forward's first answer to Norwegian broadcaster TV2 had spanned two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges after he was asked about the club's situation.

Industry observers note that 'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland remarked.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

Haaland cut a despondent figure in midweek as he admitted to 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli continued their underwhelming form.

Haaland has pushed back against suggestions the Premier League charges verdict has had an impact on Man City's form.

He continued: 'It's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

It has been revealed that 'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.'.

Haaland, who has scored 176 goals in 214 appearances for Man City, will be hoping to spark Enzo Maresca's side back into form when they face Premier League leaders Arsenal on Sunday.

Arsenal are currently six points clear of Man City heading into the match as they bid to retain their title this season.

The last international games of the year were played during the November break, so Italy, like most other countries worldwide, will return to action next year, precisely in March.

The Azzurri finished third in their Nations League group, seeing winners France and runners-up Belgium progress to the quarter-finals.

Despite the disappointment of the elimination, which experts at BetPanda had widely predicted, it is fair to say the Azzurri must see the glass half full.

Their Nations League campaign featured victories over Turkiye and France, and only their two losses to Belgium sealed the Nazionale’s elimination.

Italy, however, still managed to secure a spot among the seeded teams in the Euro 2028 qualifying draw thanks to their Nations League results.

It has been revealed that as previously mentioned, the next international break is in March 2027, running from Monday 22 to Tuesday 30. As the Azzurri won’t be playing in the Nations League quarter-finals, they’ll start their Euro 2028 qualifying campaign straight away.

Industry observers note that italy will learn their opponents on December 6, when the qualifying draw takes place. The first match will be played on March 26, 2027 and the second on March 29. The Azzurri will likely be placed in one of the four-team qualifying groups after their elimination from the Nations League.

Regardless of their opponents, the Azzurri will look to start their qualification campaign strongly and bounce back after a 4-1 loss to Belgium in their most recent match.

“These nights can happen in the growth process; you need to learn from these experiences. Considering the way we got here, we had the chance to qualify, but we knew it would be tough, as Belgium are a strong team,” Mancini said at full time in Belgium.

“We are sad, but this night will help us going forward.”.

Sources indicate that mancini returned for a second spell as Italy’s head coach in July. He has grabbed three wins, one draw and two defeats in his first six games in charge in his second spell. The Euro 2020 winner has signed a contract until 2030, when, hopefully, he’ll bring the Nazionale back to the World Cup.

Italy already know that their captain Gianluigi Donnarumma will miss the next international match after being booked in the most recent match against Belgium.

Gigio was one yellow card away from suspension prior to the game in Belgium, so he’ll miss the next one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham revealed deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.
  • This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham revealed deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham said the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that "This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham mentioned.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa said the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He said jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

Industry observers note that burnham noted that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

He went further and remarked "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up newly introduced opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen remarked the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

She said the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also remarked Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

Burnham said the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

In September, Burnham remarked he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

"Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham stated as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:.

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

According to recent reports, no deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on challenges including on tuition fees," Burnham noted.

Von der Leyen ‌said ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

Sources indicate that on the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders remarked they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other challenges.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

On Monday, Burnham remarked it ​was the "obvious truth" that ‌Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit.

Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.

Since mid-2022, a majority of people surveyed remarked Britain was wrong to leave.In September, the "Bregret" camp rose to 60% — the highest ever.

Germany, who finished top of Group A2 following their 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday are to face Belgium in the Nations League quarterfinals — after they finished second in Group A1. The Belgians recently came up with a statement result of their own, beating Italy 4-1. The match-up between the neighboring countries promises to be closely contested, with Belgium sitting at No. 8 in the men's rankings, three places above Germany.

The head coach of Belgium is former Bayern Munich player Mark van Bommel, who took over from Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual champions Spain in the quarterfinals.

Germany head into the knockout phase on a high note, not only because they won their group, but also the way they performed in their last two matches, against Serbia and the Netherlands in the group stage.

In a recent development, germany head coach Jürgen Klopp followed the draw, held in Nyon on Friday, from the German FA's (DFB) Frankfurt offices. He played down the notion that Germany enter the tie as the favorites.

"I've practically never given it any thought. It's never interested me," he said.

Recent findings suggest that "An awful lot can happen in that time. We're very happy with the final impression we left, yet we're also fully aware that we're only at the very beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive momentum forward—there's still a great deal to be done.".

The matches are slated for March 25 and March 30, 2027, and having won their group, Germany will have home-field advantage for the second leg.

Germany and Belgium have faced each other 26 times to date, with West Germany and Germany having the upper hand with 20 wins, five defeats and one draw.

Should Germany advance to the semifinals, they will go on to face the winner of England and Norway, a World Cup quarterfinals rematch.

In the other two semifinals matchups, the Netherlands drew Portugal, while the top pairing sees Spain face France in a rematch of one of last summer's World Cup semifinals.

The "Final Four" mini tournament is to be held from June 9 to 13 but the host venue won't be determined until the semifinal lineup has been completed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea star Cole Palmer has been the subject of criticism from ex-Blue Pat Nevin, who has admitted it’s getting harder to keep making excuses for him.

Palmer’s noticeable dip in form has been well-documented, with the England international not contributing nearly as much as he did in his first two seasons at Stamford Bridge.

Nevin has reluctantly admitted he’s concerned about Palmer, as enough time has passed now that the former Manchester City man can’t keep relying on excuses like coming back from an injury or playing in an unfamiliar role.

Speaking to Simon Phillips, Nevin expressed his concern about Palmer and attempted to explain what might have gone wrong for the 24-year-old.

According to recent reports, “There is a concern over Cole Palmer, I have to admit, though I hate admitting it. He was injured for large periods of last season, so he’s been going through injury recovery. You give him a slight pass for that.

“Then he was playing slightly out of position because Enzo Fernandez was in a central position, so you think that’s probably why he was peripheral.

According to recent reports, “But, can we stop this now? Can we actually say: ‘Cole, you’ve got to do it mate, it’s time now. It’s time to get back to that player that you were, controlling situations and doing genius things again.’.

Recent findings suggest that want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

According to recent reports, “It feels as if I’m always making excuses for Cole at the moment, but in the end, the numbers start telling you. Is he overthinking it? Because when Cole is at his very best, you can tell it’s completely off the cuff.

“There’s something about young players when they come through, it’s a bit easier because you act on instinct. Sometimes that instinct goes because you overthink or because you’re over-coached.

Recent findings suggest that “There are technical demands put on you like: ‘You must go to that part of the pitch.’ Well, wait a minute, maybe that’s not where I feel most dangerous in this game. I’d love to get inside the head of Cole Palmer, but it doesn’t look like an easy place to get inside, if I’m honest.

“Has he got the quality and skills to come back and be that player again? Yeah, of course he has. It’s a bit like Phil Foden, player of the year, amazing stuff, and then he had a complete period where he couldn’t score or create a great deal.

According to recent reports, “It was hard to understand how that was even possible, but you can get it back. Phil’s doing well again now, and Cole can do it as well.

“The one thing I would underline is that it has nothing to do with being left out of the England squad. That’s absolutely not the case. Looking at Cole Palmer, there is no way he can blame England, Thomas Tuchel, or anything like that. Absolutely not.”.

It’s hard to know precisely what Palmer needs right now, but it’s been a generally chaotic period at Chelsea and that probably hasn’t helped him.

Palmer’s best form came under Mauricio Pochettino in his first season in west London, and since then he’s played under three different managers, not including caretaker or interim managers.

This is far from ideal for Palmer and many would argue he’s not the only one in this CFC squad struggling to perform at their best.

Fresh manager Xabi Alonso has not quite had the desired impact yet and that’s been an matter for a few players in this squad, such as Estevao Willian and pretty much the entire defence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Large regions of chromosomes are organized into a state known as heterochromatin. This densely packed form of DNA represses gene activity. Curiously, some families of clustered genes can be activated even though they are packed as heterochromatin. Writing in Nature, Buckley et al.1 report findings that explain this paradox: they show how opposing mechanisms that control the organization of heterochromatin promote the stochastic activation of genes in the protocadherin (Pcdh) gene cluster, thereby supporting proper nervous-system development.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Premier League is set to introduce a newly introduced LGBTQ+ inclusion campaign after ending its partnership with Stonewall, the charity behind the widely recognised Rainbow Laces initiative.

Recent findings suggest that stonewallâs Rainbow Laces campaign, introduced in 2013, became a fixture across English football, with players from all Premier League clubs wearing rainbow-coloured laces and captains donning rainbow armbands to promote acceptance and equality. The campaign aimed to support LGBTQ+ rights and foster inclusivity among fans and young people.

After over a decade of collaboration, the league will now lead its own campaign, timed to coincide with LGBTQ+ History Month in February, The Telegraph report.

"Rainbow Laces has benefited from a wide range of partners with a natural ebb and flow reflecting cultural and sporting changes," a Stonewall spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"Alongside other sporting bodies the FA has been instrumental in advancing LGBTQ+ inclusion at the grassroots level and more recently the Women's Super League has taken up the mantle as the women's game has grown - enabling Rainbow Laces to reach more diverse audiences.".

Despite Stonewall's efforts, recent reports from Kick It Out reveal an alarming increase in discriminatory incidents in football, including rises in sexism, transphobia and faith-based abuse, with racism continuing to be the most prevalent glitch.

It has been revealed that controversies around playersâ attitudes to rainbow armbands have also made headlines. Last season, Ipswich captain Sam Morsy declined to wear one due to religious beliefs, while Crystal Palaceâs Marc GuÃ©hi faced criticism for personalising his armband with the phrase âI Love Jesus.â.

Additionally, Manchester United scrapped plans for LGBTQ+ support jackets after a player refused to participate.

With no openly gay or bisexual players currently in the Premier League, and the surge in discriminatory incidents, some question the timing of the split from Stonewall â an organisation highly respected for its work in LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Details of the Premier Leagueâs newly introduced campaign are still under wraps, but as the league presses âreset,â thereâs hope it will introduce a meaningful and effective initiative that advances equality rather than undermines it.
