Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2245 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that LATEST YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.
  • "I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune said post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".
  • It has been revealed that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that LATEST YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune said post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

It has been revealed that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game plan that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Latest York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

It has been revealed that "We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins said. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

Industry observers note that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness concerns over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

"I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill remarked. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two notable blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of New York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

In the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas said. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match plan that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

It has been revealed that the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

Sources indicate that "Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a blueprint," Armas said. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

In a recent development, gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while presently headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros stated. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up proposal for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull Upcoming York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

Recent findings suggest that "I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce noted. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

The Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

Recent findings suggest that "I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros said. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

"Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

  • Two-thirds of the world’s population will be living in cities by 2050, according to the latest estimates by the United Nations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aerial scenery of Hengqin Free Trade Zone, China. Credit: Weiming Xie/Shutterstock.

Two-thirds of the world’s population will be living in cities by 2050, according to the latest estimates by the United Nations. Coinciding with the mass movement of people into urban areas is the rapid integration of technology into many of those spaces. From automated subterranean waste-collection systems to driverless vehicle zones, these ‘smart-city’ solutions are changing the way that people live, work and move through their environments.

Some cities are embracing these technological advances at a much faster pace than others. Places such as Beijing, Helsinki, London and Singapore stand out for the way they are integrating smart-city technology into existing infrastructure and services.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

According to recent reports, other cities are emerging with these technologies integral to their operations from their inception. But as the examples of Songdo in South Korea and Hengqin in China illustrate, building smart infrastructure from scratch is only half the challenge: these places must also attract and retain the research and innovation talent needed to develop, operate and improve it. It’s a ‘chicken-and-egg’ problem, indicates Songdo-based urban-planning researcher, Dakota McCarty: talent follows world-class universities and thriving economic zones, which need a critical mass of expertise and investment to be attractive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Espanyol beat Athletic Club 1-0 in Bilbao through a Roberto Fernández goal. The result extends a strong run since Manolo González left and leaves Athletic seventh after a home defeat in which they dominated the statistics.

A crowd of 46,107 was at San Mamés on Friday 20 November 2026. The fixture opened Matchday 13 of LaLiga EA Sports.

The win was Eder Sarabia’s second in charge of Espanyol and his second in a row away from home. The club have now taken seven of the nine points available since González left, according to EFE. Espanyol named Sarabia head coach on 28 October 2026, on a contract that runs until 2028.

His appointment followed a 4-3 Copa del Rey defeat at Sestao River. A 1-0 win at Villarreal, a 0-0 draw with Deportivo La Coruna and Friday’s victory in Bilbao make up Espanyol’s results since González’s exit. Their goal difference now stands at zero.

Industry observers note that the first half ended goalless. Tyrhys Dolan replaced Pere Milla in the 57th minute. Sarabia also sent on Gabriel Moscardó and Javi Hernández in the 65th minute.

Recent findings suggest that A minute later, Dolan set up Fernández for the winner. It was the striker’s sixth league goal of the season, putting him eighth in the LaLiga scoring list. He finished with 3 shots and a rating of 7.92.

Industry observers note that sarabia then brought on Unai Núñez and Javi Puado in the 84th minute to protect the lead. Clemens Riedel was booked in the third minute of stoppage time, Espanyol’s only card of the night.

Goalkeeper Ángel Fortuño made six saves to keep a clean sheet.

In a recent development, the result gave Espanyol a third successive league win over Athletic. They won 2-0 at home on 13 May 2026 and 2-1 at San Mamés on 22 December 2025.

Athletic controlled most of the statistics. They had 58% of possession and 9 corners to Espanyol’s 2. On target, the hosts had 6 efforts and the visitors 3.

Edin Terzić moved away from the 4-4-2 he had used in previous matches to fit Oihan Sancet into a 4-2-3-1. The change did not produce more attacking threat. Deia judged this to be Athletic’s worst performance at San Mamés since Terzić took charge.

Nico Williams had 5 shots and 3 key passes. Iñigo Ruiz de Galarreta also created 3 chances in 29 minutes on the pitch. Athletic collected three yellow cards, for Iñaki Williams, Ruiz de Galarreta and Yeray Álvarez.

Athletic fall to defeat at San Mames.#AthleticEspanyol #AthleticClub 🦁 pic.twitter.com/tRnTpjuX14.

— Athletic Club (@Athletic_en) November 20, 2026.

Before kick-off, San Mamés paid tribute to Elene Gurtubay and Daniela Agote, who won the Under-20 World Cup.

After 12 matches, Terzić’s side have 16 points. Their recent run reads one draw, two wins and one defeat in the league before Friday’s loss. Real Sociedad sit fifth on 22 points.

It has been revealed that athletic travel to bottom side Malaga on Saturday 28 November. Espanyol host Getafe on Monday 30 November.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino stated he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

It has been revealed that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

"For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that says it's not key tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his plans for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

"What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the latest coaches that arrive here," Pochettino said. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

In a recent development, for all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

For perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an notable new chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

According to recent reports, as for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his fresh role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

Two years removed from starting a upcoming job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-crucial clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, it's not difficult," he said of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most crucial [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are at the moment in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, substitute Carlos Espí struck late as Real Madrid came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabéu. The result keeps Madrid firmly in the title race with Barcelona.

The victory over Celta on Saturday 21 November 2026 was Madrid’s ninth in a row. It also kept their 100% home record this season intact.

Recent findings suggest that the winner began with a Vinícius Júnior cross. Espí headed it, Celta goalkeeper Ionuț Radu saved, and the striker scored from the rebound in the six-yard box. He had been on the pitch for only a few minutes.

Espí had played only 44 minutes of LaLiga football this season before kick-off, according to ESPN. All three of his league goals have now won games, against Espanyol, Elche and Celta. He also scored in the 4-3 Champions League comeback win at Roma. The goal was his fourth of the season, the club stated.

Espí called his first goal in front of the Bernabéu crowd his most special for the club. José Mourinho described him as a pure penalty-box striker. The coach added that football history has many players like him who decide games without playing many minutes.

Pablo Durán gave Celta a sixth-minute lead from a Williot Swedberg pass. Kylian Mbappé then missed a penalty in the 39th minute, and the visitors led 1-0 at the break.

Mourinho had started Vinícius and Federico Valverde on the bench. He sent them on with Marc Cucurella in the second half to chase the game. Thibaut Courtois kept Madrid in it with a strong low save from a long-range Durán shot in the 65th minute. A minute later, Jude Bellingham equalised from an Mbappé assist.

The figures show how one-sided the contest was. Madrid had 24 shots to Celta’s 8 and an expected goals total of 3.8 against 1.52. Radu made five saves, and the hosts held 64% of possession.

Sources indicate that celta coach Claudio Giráldez mentioned Madrid’s substitutes had decided the game. He pointed out that he had started six academy graduates. Many of his players were appearing at the Bernabéu for the first time. Giráldez replaced Hugo Álvarez with Ferran Jutglà at half-time and sent on Iago Aspas for Durán in the 76th minute. Celta are 13th on 13 points.

Sources indicate that barcelona still top the table on goal difference, 35 to 22. They can move clear again when they host Villarreal on Sunday 22 November.

In the LaLiga scoring chart, Mbappé is second with 13 goals. Barcelona’s Raphinha leads on 15.

📞 Just call Carlos Espí. #LaLigaHighlights pic.twitter.com/z9KqjfkhmY.

— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 21, 2026.

In a recent development, earlier on Saturday, Rafael Nadal was elected to Real Madrid’s board of directors at an Extraordinary General Assembly at Ciudad Real Madrid. Later, he watched the game from the stands and was visibly emotional.

Sources indicate that celta host Bournemouth in the Europa League at Balaídos on Thursday 26 November, with 3 points from four games. Madrid face PSV in the Champions League at the Bernabéu on Tuesday 24 November at 20:00 UTC. They have won all four of their league-phase games and sit second on 12 points, while PSV are 24th on 4 points.
